goal: Part A of issue #2662: remove the anon and authenticated Data API grants from four RLS-enabled, zero-policy public tables, so their protection no longer rests solely on an empty policy set that a later unrelated policy would silently defeat.
dispatcher: Claude shared-db lane dispatch for issue 2662
prohibited_actions: Do not touch the definer views or materialized views in the same finding; they carry an owner business judgement and are Part B, planned but not applied.
Do not add, alter or drop any RLS policy; this work removes grants only and leaves the empty policy set in place as the second layer.
Do not revoke from service_role or postgres; every live writer of these tables is server-side and must keep working.
Do not run direct production DDL, and do not weaken any guard to make a check pass.
assumptions: All four tables have RLS enabled with zero policies, so anon and authenticated are already denied and removing their grants changes no behaviour today.
The only live traffic to these tables is service-role, which bypasses RLS and is untouched by this migration.

Production promotion is a separate governed gate after merge, not part of this contract; it needs the owner to name the exact resource and action, so this lane delivers only as far as guarded merge and preview.
stop_conditions: Stop if any of the four tables is found to have a policy, since revoking the grant would then remove access something actually relies on.
Stop if production edge logs show any browser anon or authenticated caller succeeding against any of the four tables, since the revoke would then be a breaking change rather than a tightening.
Stop if any of the four tables turns out to be shared with an object under another active claim on this issue.
